Recommendation 2's contextual notes on known or suspected primary neoplasm and active infection are not executable conditions here.

provenance.locator: General nodule measurement note: use the average of long- and short-axis diameters rounded to the nearest whole millimeter. This convention governs the clinician's set-level fleischner_multiple_solid_all_lt_6mm=false attestation on GR-7; no per-lesion engine measurement or volume-equivalent logic is introduced.

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner (2017) Recommendation 2 and Table 1A recommend an initial CT follow-up at 3-6 months for multiple solid noncalcified pulmonary nodules found incidentally when at least one nodule is 6 mm or larger — in both the 6-8 mm and the >8 mm columns and for both low- and high-risk patients — in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. This rule applies only to multiple discrete/circumscribed nodules whose set is solid-only, at initial assessment, with at least one nodule 6 mm or larger by the Fleischner whole-nodule average-diameter convention. Fleischner notes that management may instead be guided by a larger or more suspicious nodule according to its solitary-nodule recommendations, and that the most suspicious nodule is not necessarily the largest; this recommendation applies only because the clinician has confirmed that no individual larger or more suspicious nodule currently requires such management. No index, largest, dominant, or most-suspicious nodule is identified, ranked, or selected by this application, and no Fleischner risk category is collected or used. This recommendation covers only the first follow-up CT: the risk-dependent CT at 18-24 months, solitary-nodule-directed management of any individual nodule, PET/CT, biopsy, and resection are outside this Rule-Set Release and must not be inferred from it.
